exact_statement: For nearest-neighbor FPP on Z^2 with iid edge weights identically equal to 1, the path (k,0), k in Z, is a bigeodesic.

source.ranking_quote: Absence of bi-infinite geodesics in planar iid FPP

proof_or_counterexample: Every finite horizontal subpath has length equal to the l1 distance of its endpoints; no path has fewer edges.
remaining_gap: No gap in the elementary argument identified; independent check pending. This addresses the unrestricted title only.

exact_statement: For fixed finite strictly positive weights on the nearest-neighbor Z^2 lattice, E_R (some finite geodesic between distinct vertices of the l-infinity sphere of radius R contains 0) decreases with R, and its intersection is exactly existence of a bigeodesic through 0.
assumptions: Bigeodesic means a doubly infinite simple path with all finite segments globally minimizing
proof_or_counterexample: First-exit truncation, finite witness sets inside each finite box, and an infinite branch in their truncation tree.
remaining_gap: Independent audit of truncation consistency and compactness pending; the reduction does not prove decay of P(E_R).

exact_statement: In a translation-invariant law on such environments, if along unbounded R_j the supremum q_R of origin-hit probabilities for sphere endpoint pairs satisfies (32R_j^2-4R_j)q_(R_j)->0, then almost surely there is no bigeodesic anywhere.
proof_or_counterexample: Union bound over binomial(8R,2) unordered pairs, decreasing-event continuity using C02, and countable union over lattice vertices.
remaining_gap: The quantitative estimate is unproved for the target iid FPP model; this is a conditional bridge only.

exact_statement: Uniform convergence to zero of individual probabilities in a growing family need not imply decay of the union probability, even when each is exactly 1/(32R^2-4R).
assumptions: For each R partition [0,1) into M_R=32R^2-4R equal half-open intervals
proof_or_counterexample: The M_R interval events each have probability 1/M_R; their union is the whole probability space. The union events are constant and thus nested.
remaining_gap: Independent check pending. This is a logical probability counterexample, not an iid-FPP counterexample.

exact_statement: Two finite strictly positive completions of the same B_1 weights have different globally minimizing S_1-through-origin events; the box-minimizer event is unchanged.
assumptions: First completion constant 1; second S_2 perimeter/connectors 1/20, remaining weights 1
proof_or_counterexample: Every S_1 pair has an outside bypass costing <=1/2 in the second completion, while every simple through-origin path costs >=2. Integer-weight Dijkstra checked all 28 pairs: global hit counts 16 versus 0; box counts 16 versus 16.
remaining_gap: Independent mathematical check pending; no iid-FPP counterexample is claimed.

exact_statement: For each fixed M and finite partition-independent neighborhood, distinct marked labels give eventual retention under vanishing bin diameter and hence probability convergence. Partition-dependent neighborhoods need not give it.
assumptions: For fixed M a deterministic finite neighborhood independent of partition index
Distinct labels on marked pairs almost surely
Deterministic partitions with maximal bin diameter tending to zero
All marked labels belong to a fixed compact interval I; the finite partitions cover I
proof_or_counterexample: Finitely many distinct neighbors are eventually in different bins; take the maximum separating index and apply bounded convergence. For iid uniform labels, a k-bin partition retains probability (1-1/k)^(2N); N=k^2 makes it tend to zero despite pairwise distinct labels.
remaining_gap: The cited preprint explicitly states the fixed-neighborhood premise; its upstream uniform-comparison and distinct-label theorems remain outside this local audit.
